This study evaluates various machine learning models for predicting non-performing loans (NPLs) using a dataset containing 1,000 observations. The analysis focuses on comparing model performance, identifying the most significant features, and examining feature interactions. The results indicate that the Random Forest model outperforms others, achieving an accuracy of 0.85, a precision of 0.84, a recall of 0.85, and an F1 score of 0.84. Furthermore, the analysis reveals that the "loan to value" ratio is the most critical feature, while the "loan to income" ratio ranks second.

This paper presents a combinatorial proof of the conjecture by Shareshian and Woodroofe, which establishes a link between the chromatic symmetric function of the order complex of the poset of Dyck trails and the $q$-analogue of the Eulerian numbers.

Directional Convolutional Networks (DiConv) are a new class of convolutional neural networks designed to capture directional information within images. This paper introduces DiConv, a novel convolutional layer that utilizes directional filters to extract directional features. We demonstrate that DiConv can be integrated into existing CNN architectures with minimal modifications, resulting in improved performance on image classification tasks. Specifically, we show that using DiConv layers instead of standard convolutional layers leads to better accuracy on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets. Additionally, we present a new architecture, the Directional Residual Network (DiResNet), which combines DiConv layers with residual connections. Experimental results indicate that DiResNet achieves state-of-the-art performance on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 benchmarks.

This paper establishes a curved linear period formula for $GL(2)$, which serves as a curved analogue to the linear period formula for $GL(2)$ developed by Jacquet and Shalika. We further demonstrate that this curved linear period formula is equivalent to a novel relative trace formula.

We investigate the light-flavor dependence of the top quark mass, $m_t$, within the Standard Model, specifically examining how the mass shifts when the light quark content is altered. Our findings indicate that the light quark contribution to $m_t$ is negligible, with the dominant effect arising from the bottom quark. Consequently, the top quark mass exhibits a strong dependence on the bottom quark mass, $m_b$, while remaining largely insensitive to the masses of the other light quarks.

This paper introduces a new concept called "sequential edge-tinting," which involves assigning colors to edges sequentially. We establish that for any almost regular graph $G$ with a maximum degree $\Delta(G) \leq 3$, the edges can be colored using at most $\Delta(G) + 1$ colors such that no two adjacent edges share the same color, and the coloring of any edge depends only on the colors of its neighbors. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this property holds for any graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \leq 3$ if we consider the edges to be colored sequentially based on their degree. Finally, we show that the edges of any graph $G$ with $\Delta(G) \leq 3$ can be colored using at most $\Delta(G) + 1$ colors such that no two adjacent edges share the same color, and the coloring of any edge depends only on the colors of its neighbors.
This paper establishes hypercontractive inequalities for a broad class of weighted Berman operators.

The rapid spread of the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) has caused a global pandemic, resulting in significant loss of life and economic disruption. While the virus is highly contagious, it is not always fatal, and early detection is crucial for preventing its further transmission. Although the virus primarily targets the lungs, it can also affect other organs, making it difficult to diagnose using standard clinical methods. Consequently, there is an urgent need for a reliable, non-invasive, and cost-effective diagnostic tool. This study proposes a novel deep learning framework designed to detect COVID-19 from low-dose Computed Tomography (CT) scans. The suggested architecture utilizes a two-stage Time-distributed capsule network (TDCN) to identify the virus. The first stage employs a TDCN to extract features from the CT images, while the second stage applies a TDCN to classify the extracted features. Experimental results indicate that this model achieves a 99.9% accuracy rate in detecting COVID-19 from low-dose CT scans.

This study examines the potential for space utilization in Low-Earth Orbit (LEO) by analyzing the physical and orbital characteristics of the region. It evaluates the feasibility of using LEO for space-based solar power, satellite communications, and scientific research, while also addressing the challenges of space debris and radiation. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research and development in this field.

This study introduces a novel method for creating high-order coarse meshes on CAD models, utilizing a mesh generation technique based on integer linear programming (ILP). The approach begins by defining a meshing domain through a set of linear inequalities, where the coefficients are derived from the CAD model's geometry. Subsequently, the mesh is constructed by solving the ILP problem to determine the mesh vertices. The resulting mesh exhibits high-order accuracy, with element quality that is both high and consistent. Furthermore, the method is highly efficient, capable of generating meshes for complex CAD models in a matter of seconds.

This study derives formulas for the sample moments of the sample correlation coefficient, calculated across all possible permutations of a dataset. These formulas are expressed as functions of the sample size, the sample moments of the correlation coefficient, and the sample moments of the underlying data.

We introduce a general gravity framework that extends the $S$-matrix method to arbitrary dimensions and arbitrary spins. This approach is built upon the principle that the $S$-matrix must be Lorentz invariant, unitary, and causal. By applying these constraints, we derive the general gravity action, which encompasses Einstein-Hilbert gravity as a specific case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the resulting equations of motion are equivalent to the standard Einstein equations.

This study examines the uniform stabilization of the Navier-Stokes equations within critical Sobolev and Besov spaces defined by $L^q$-based norms. We demonstrate that a finite-dimensional, localized, interior feedback control law can stabilize these equations in the critical Sobolev space $H^{s_c}_q = W^{s_c,q}(\mathbb{T}^3)$ and the critical Besov space $B^{s_c}_{q,q}(\mathbb{T}^3)$, where the critical regularity index is given by $s_c = \frac{3}{q} - 1$. Furthermore, we establish that the feedback gain required for stabilization remains independent of the initial data's magnitude.

LitMind Lexicon is an open-source online dictionary designed to support the LitMind platform, a digital humanities project dedicated to the study of classical Chinese literature. It provides comprehensive entries for classical Chinese characters, including their definitions, pronunciations, and usage examples.

Explainable recommendation systems (RecSys) are essential for assisting users in making informed decisions and for enabling developers to identify and rectify biases within their models. However, current explainability methods often fail to align with the specific needs of both users and developers. This paper introduces a novel framework for generating explanations for RecSys, grounded in the concept of "adherence." Adherence refers to the degree to which a model's predictions are consistent with a user's or developer's specific expectations. We demonstrate that adherence is a critical factor in RecSys and propose a new method for generating explanations that explicitly incorporates these user-defined expectations.

This study examines the Fermi level pinning phenomenon in InAs quantum wells (QWs) situated near the surface of InP substrates. We demonstrate that the pinning effect can be mitigated by employing a thin, undoped InAs spacer layer between the QW and the substrate. Furthermore, we show that the pinning effect can be reversed by introducing a thin, doped InAs spacer layer between the QW and the substrate.

This study investigates the utility of local inquiries in robust learning, where an adversary can corrupt a fraction of training data. We demonstrate that for any hypothesis class, the sample complexity of robust learning is equivalent to that of standard learning augmented by the number of local inquiries required to achieve a specific accuracy. Furthermore, we establish that this equivalence holds even when inquiries are restricted to a single query per example.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for efficiently and accurately calculating the optimal transport cost between two discrete measures. The approach leverages a specific triangular matrix structure, which is a variation of the collinear transport problem, to achieve a linear time complexity of $O(n)$. The algorithm's performance is validated through numerical experiments, demonstrating its speed and precision.

The data reveal that the star's FUV emission is dominated by a strong, variable stellar wind, with a weaker, more stable coronal component. The wind's variability is characterized by a 100% fluctuation in flux over a 10-day period, driven by a 100% change in wind density. The coronal component remains relatively constant, varying by only 10% over the same timeframe. The wind's spectral profile exhibits a blue shift of 100 km/s, indicating a high-velocity outflow. This study examines the impact of a resistive material medium on the radiation reaction force acting on a charged particle. We demonstrate that the medium induces a drag force on the particle, which is proportional to the particle's velocity.

This study investigates the classification of imbalanced datasets using a statistical approach. We demonstrate that the optimal classifier for such data is the Closest Neighbor (CN) method, which assigns a class label based on the majority class among the $k$ nearest neighbors. We further establish that the CN classifier is asymptotically optimal, meaning it achieves the lowest possible error rate. Additionally, we derive an analytical formula for the error rate of the CN classifier, which is validated through numerical experiments.

We present a new sample of 108 quasars with redshifts exceeding 2.5, identified through the SkyMapper Southern Survey. These objects were selected based on their high apparent magnitudes (r < 19.5) and confirmed via spectroscopy. The resulting sample is the most luminous and redshifted collection of quasars observed to date, with a mean redshift of 3.02 and a mean absolute magnitude of -27.1. We have calculated the luminosity function for this sample, which extends to the brightest end of the distribution. The data indicate that the luminosity function's slope steepens significantly at high luminosities, with a break occurring around -27.5. Furthermore, we have determined the evolution of the luminosity function up to z = 3.02, finding that the most luminous quasars evolve more rapidly than those with lower luminosities.

We present a quantum dot system designed to detect charge tunneling events between a quantum dot and a superconducting island. This setup enables the investigation of how the superconducting island's charge state influences the quantum dot's energy spectrum. By employing a gate sensor, we successfully resolve the quantum dot's spectral lines for both the neutral and singly charged states of the superconducting island. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the gate sensor can detect the quantum dot's charge state, even when the tunneling rate is significantly slower than the gate sensor's response time.

This paper introduces a new contraction principle for systems of conservation laws featuring discontinuous entropy solutions. We establish a contraction metric that ensures the distance between any two entropy solutions decreases over time, measured within a specific Riemannian metric space. This approach extends the contraction principle originally developed by Bressan and Colombo for smooth solutions to the contraction framework proposed by Colombo and De Lellis for entropy solutions.

Perpetual view synthesis aims to generate novel views of a scene from a single input image. While recent methods utilizing 3D Gaussian Splatting have shown promise, they often suffer from artifacts and hallucinations, particularly in regions lacking data. To address this, we introduce DiffDreamer, a novel approach leveraging conditional diffusion models to produce high-fidelity perpetual views. Our method employs a two-stage pipeline: first, a 3D Gaussian Splatting model generates an initial view, which is then refined by the diffusion model to correct artifacts and hallucinations. We further enhance performance by incorporating a multi-scale conditioning strategy and a multi-view consistency loss. Extensive experiments demonstrate that DiffDreamer achieves superior visual quality compared to state-of-the-art methods.

This study introduces a data-driven approach to model, optimize, and control networked systems, specifically focusing on the Susceptible-Infected-Susceptible (SIS) epidemic model. We propose a framework that utilizes a data-driven method to forecast the evolution of the SIS process, a technique that requires no prior knowledge of the network's topology or the underlying dynamics. Furthermore, we develop an optimization strategy to determine the optimal control policy for the SIS process, relying solely on data. The efficacy of this framework is validated through simulations on both synthetic and real-world networks.

This study examines the Rayleigh-Plateau instability of a liquid film coating a solid fiber, where the fiber's surface is characterized by a periodic slip length. The analysis employs a perturbation approach, expanding the governing equations in powers of the film's aspect ratio. The resulting linearized equations are solved using a Fourier series, with the slip length treated as a periodic function. The findings indicate that the slip length significantly influences the instability's growth rate and the wavelength of the emerging drops. Furthermore, the study reveals that the instability's wavelength is highly sensitive to the slip length's period, exhibiting a periodic dependence on this parameter.

This study establishes the Lipschitz stability of the Hunter-Saxton model, a nonlinear hyperbolic partial differential equation that models the evolution of curvature in a string. The analysis demonstrates that the Lipschitz continuity of the solution with respect to the initial data holds under the condition that the initial curvature remains bounded.

This study investigates the reliability of robotic ultrasound imaging for scoliosis assessment, contrasting it with manual scanning. The research involved 100 participants, including 50 scoliosis patients and 50 healthy controls, who underwent both manual and robotic ultrasound examinations. The manual scans were performed by two independent sonographers, while the robotic scans were executed by a single operator. The resulting images were analyzed using the Cobb angle method. The findings indicate that the inter-rater reliability of manual scans was moderate, whereas the intra-rater reliability for robotic scans was high. Furthermore, the inter-rater reliability of the robotic scans was significantly superior to that of the manual scans. These results suggest that robotic ultrasound imaging offers a more reliable approach for scoliosis assessment compared to manual techniques.

This study introduces a non-parametric method for generating synthetic speech durations, designed to enhance the performance of speech recognition systems. The proposed approach utilizes a median-based technique to synthesize durations from a given set of phonetic units. The effectiveness of this method was evaluated by training a Hidden Markov Model (HMM) speech recognizer using synthetic durations derived from the TIMIT database. The results indicate that the proposed method outperforms existing techniques, achieving a 1.5% reduction in word error rate (WER) compared to the baseline.

This study introduces a feature selection-based model designed to identify hate speech. We evaluated the performance of various feature selection methods, including Chi-Square, Information Gain, and Mutual Information, to determine the most effective approach. The selected features were subsequently utilized to train a Naive Bayes classifier. Experimental results indicate that the proposed model achieves a 99.9% accuracy rate, a 99.9% precision rate, and a 99.9% recall rate.

This study introduces a novel Multi-Input Multi-Output (MIMO) architecture designed for image classification, featuring a dual-branch structure that shares features across two parallel pathways. The first branch employs a standard convolutional neural network (CNN), while the second utilizes a MIMO network. The model's output is derived from a weighted combination of the final representations from both branches. Experimental results on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets demonstrate that this architecture achieves superior accuracy compared to existing state-of-the-art methods.

This paper provides a comprehensive survey of publicly available historical manuscript image datasets, which are essential for advancing research in the field. We examine the characteristics of these datasets, including their content, format, and resolution, and outline the primary research areas enabled by them. Furthermore, we analyze the methodologies employed in their creation and discuss the specific challenges and limitations inherent to each. Finally, we identify key future research directions and propose potential avenues for further investigation.

This study presents a flatness-based control strategy for regulating an industrial robot joint, utilizing secondary encoders to measure the link's angular velocity. The approach involves designing a state observer to estimate the joint's position and velocity, which are then fed into a flatness-based controller. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior performance compared to a standard PD controller.

This study introduces a multidimensional framework for analyzing multiple time-to-event data, specifically designed to capture the complex, dynamic health trajectories of patients with myocardial infarction (MI). The proposed model integrates multiple states, allowing for the simultaneous analysis of recurrent events, transitions between health states, and the duration spent in each state. By employing a flexible, non-parametric baseline hazard function, the model accommodates intricate dependencies among these processes. Furthermore, it enables the investigation of how various risk factors influence the underlying hazard rates for each state. The methodology is illustrated using data from the Cardiovascular Health Study, focusing on the health progression of individuals with MI.

This study introduces a multi-center integration approach for solving the molecular Schrödinger equation, designed to enhance the efficiency of multi-configuration time-dependent Hartree-Fock (MCTDHF) simulations. The method employs a grid of Gaussian-type basis functions centered on each atomic nucleus, with the total wave function constructed as a linear combination of these basis functions. To address the discontinuities in the wave function's second derivative at the nuclear positions, the integration scheme utilizes a specialized technique that incorporates the nuclear Coulomb potential directly into the integration process. The authors demonstrate that this approach significantly improves computational efficiency compared to standard methods, particularly for systems with multiple nuclei. The method is validated by applying it to the calculation of the ground state energy of the H$_2$ molecule, showing excellent agreement with benchmark results. The authors conclude that this multi-center integration scheme offers a robust and efficient framework for solving the molecular Schrödinger equation, with broad applicability to various molecular systems.

The metric dimension of a graph $G$ is defined as the smallest possible size of a resolving set for $G$. This study investigates the parameterized complexity of determining whether a graph $G$ possesses a resolving set of size at most $k$, focusing on structural parameters such as the minimum number of vertices to remove to yield a forest (feedback vertex set), the minimum number of edges to remove to yield a forest (feedback edge set), and the minimum number of edges to remove to yield a star forest (feedback star set). We demonstrate that the metric dimension problem is fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) when parameterized by the feedback vertex set, feedback edge set, or feedback star set. Furthermore, we establish that the metric dimension is W[1]-hard when parameterized by the feedback star set.

This paper introduces a power framework for directed spaces, a concept previously developed by the authors in [1] for topological spaces. We demonstrate that this directed power framework is both directed and continuous, and we establish a directed version of the power theorem found in [1].

This study examines the precipitation patterns of a simulated hothouse Earth, characterized by a 100% cloud cover and a 100% relative humidity atmosphere. The results indicate that while the mean precipitation rate remains constant, the temporal distribution is highly skewed, featuring a long tail of rare, intense downpours. These events are driven by the stochastic nature of cloud droplet coalescence, which creates a heavy-tailed distribution of raindrop sizes. Consequently, the total rainfall is dominated by these infrequent, high-intensity episodes. The research further demonstrates that the statistical properties of this precipitation regime are independent of the specific cloud microphysics, provided the atmosphere maintains a state of 100% relative humidity.

We introduce a twistor-based framework for extending self-dual Yang-Mills theory to arbitrary spin, utilizing a higher-spin generalization of the Penrose transform. This approach yields a higher-spin analogue of the Ward correspondence, which establishes a link between self-dual Yang-Mills configurations and connections on a principal bundle defined over the flag manifold.

Label noise is a prevalent issue in medical image classification, often stemming from the inherent subjectivity of human annotators. This study introduces a Bayesian statistics-driven label rejuvenation mechanism designed to mitigate such noise. The approach leverages Bayesian inference to calculate the probability of a label being correct, subsequently updating noisy labels based on these probabilities. Experimental results on two medical image datasets demonstrate that this method significantly enhances classification accuracy.

This paper examines the norm of an interpolation projector $P$ defined on the space $C[a,b]$, where $P$ interpolates a function $f$ at the zeros of the polynomial $Q$ of degree $n$ satisfying the differential equation $Q^{(n)}(x) = \exp(x)$. The study derives an asymptotic estimate for the norm of $P$ as $n$ approaches infinity.

This paper introduces a novel characteristic polynomial for the transition probability matrix of a random walk on a graph, defined as the product of the eigenvalues of the graph's adjacency matrix and the eigenvalues of a specific matrix $M$. The matrix $M$ is constructed from the graph's degree matrix and a diagonal matrix containing the reciprocals of the degrees of its vertices.

This paper introduces a novel approach to defining timed systems within the HOL theorem prover. By utilizing a new type of definition, we can specify the behavior of such systems through a set of equations. We demonstrate that this method is applicable to various examples, including a simple circuit, a traffic light controller, and a bus system.

This study introduces a data-driven approach to refine the wall turbulence model developed by coherant structure-based methods. The original model, which relies on the instantaneous streamwise velocity gradient and wall-normal vorticity, was enhanced by incorporating a third input variable. This new variable was identified through a data-driven technique that analyzes the relationship between the model's prediction errors and the instantaneous turbulent flow field. The resulting model demonstrates significant improvements in predicting the instantaneous streamwise velocity within the near-wall region of a turbulent channel flow.

We investigate the existence of self-dual solitons within a Born-Infeld variant of the Skyrme model, which incorporates a mass term and a Skyrme term. Our findings reveal that the model supports both self-dual and anti-self-dual solitons, with the latter being unstable. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Skyrme term is essential for the stability of these self-dual configurations.

We investigate the Hofstadter effect within a honeycomb lattice featuring a staggered sublattice potential and a staggered sublattice magnetization. Our analysis reveals that the system exhibits a Weyl metal phase characterized by time-reversal symmetry breaking. In this phase, the Weyl nodes are positioned at the Brillouin zone corners, and their chirality is dictated by the magnetization direction. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the system supports chiral edge states, which are robust against backscattering.

This study introduces a hybrid dielectric-plasmonic nanoantenna designed to function as a highly efficient, luminous, and unidirectional single-photon source. The device consists of a gold plasmonic bowtie antenna integrated with a silicon dielectric bowtie, with a quantum dot positioned at the center. The plasmonic component ensures strong light-matter interaction, while the dielectric element enhances radiation efficiency and directs emission. Theoretical analysis indicates that the nanoantenna achieves a quantum yield of 90% and a directional emission ratio of 95%. Furthermore, the system supports a tunable emission wavelength ranging from 600 to 1000 nm, with a narrow spectral linewidth of 10 nm.

This study presents an experimental and numerical validation of the anomalous screening theory for granular matter, which was originally proposed by the authors in 2019. The experiments were conducted using a 2D granular assembly within a rotating drum, where the system's response to an external electric field was measured. The results demonstrate that the theory accurately predicts the system's behavior, providing strong evidence for its validity.

This study examines the electronic properties of Mn-decorated silicene supported by hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) using first-principles calculations. The results indicate that the Mn atom binds to the silicene surface with a binding energy of 1.02 eV, resulting in a magnetic moment of 4.98 $\mu_B$. Furthermore, the Mn atom induces a magnetic exchange splitting of 0.11 eV within the silicene band structure, creating a half-metallic state.

Sgr A East is a compact radio source situated near the Galactic Center, characterized by a complex morphology and a high-velocity shell expanding at approximately 1000 km/s. This study investigates the origin of Sgr A East by modeling its evolution as a supernova remnant (SNR) interacting with a dense, inhomogeneous medium. We employed a 3D hydrodynamical simulation to track the interaction between the SNR and the surrounding environment, utilizing the resulting density and temperature distributions to generate synthetic X-ray and radio spectra. These synthetic spectra were then compared against observational data from Chandra and VLA. Our analysis indicates that the best fit is achieved when the progenitor star explodes within a dense molecular cloud core, specifically at a density of roughly $10^4$ cm$^{-3}$. This scenario aligns with the hypothesis that the remnant formed from a Type II-P supernova occurring within a dense star-forming region.

This study evaluates the efficacy of various over-sampling methods for multi-class text classification. We assess the performance of SMOTE, SMOTE-NC, and a newly proposed technique, SMOTE-NC-Text, across three distinct datasets. Our findings indicate that SMOTE-NC-Text outperforms both SMOTE and SMOTE-NC in terms of classification accuracy.

This study examines the relationship between COVID-19 coverage in U.S. local news and the pandemic's impact on cases, fatalities, and audience engagement. Utilizing data from 1,000 local news outlets, we analyzed 1.2 million articles published between January 2020 and May 2021. Our findings indicate that news coverage is positively correlated with both case counts and death tolls, yet negatively associated with audience engagement. Furthermore, the study reveals that the volume of news coverage is significantly higher in areas with greater racial and ethnic diversity.

The Fast Multipole Method (FMM) is a highly efficient algorithm for solving the Poisson equation, particularly when applied to large-scale problems. However, it is not inherently designed to conserve angular momentum. This study presents a novel FMM-based solver that explicitly conserves angular momentum. The approach involves decomposing the total angular momentum into contributions from individual particles and the multipole expansion coefficients. By deriving the corresponding equations of motion for these coefficients, the solver ensures the conservation of angular momentum. The method's efficacy is demonstrated through simulations of a collapsing cloud of particles, where the results are compared against those obtained using a standard FMM solver.

This study examines the polarization transfer from an incident proton to a recoil proton in the elastic scattering process $e\vec{p} \to e\vec{p}$. The analysis focuses on the kinematic regime where the initial proton polarization is high, the momentum transfer is substantial, and the scattering angle is large. The investigation utilizes the polarization transfer coefficients $K_i$ and $L_i$ ($i=1,2,3$), which are expressed as functions of the scattering angle and the ratio of the four-momentum transfer squared to the square of the beam energy. The study also explores the sensitivity of these coefficients to the proton's electromagnetic form factors.

Parametric experts are a popular approach for modeling complex functions, particularly in scenarios where data is scarce. However, their training is often hindered by the need for large datasets, which are difficult to obtain. This paper introduces a data augmentation strategy designed to improve the training of parametric experts. The proposed method generates synthetic data by sampling from the model's prior distribution and applying the model itself. We demonstrate that this augmentation technique significantly boosts performance across various tasks, including regression, classification, and density estimation.

This study examines the production of Higgs boson pairs alongside a vector boson ($V$) in proton-proton collisions at the Large Hadron Collider, utilizing data from the ATLAS detector. The analysis covers a dataset corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 139 fb$^{-1}$ collected at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV. The investigation focuses on the $VV$ decay channel, where $V$ represents either a $W$ or $Z$ boson, and the Higgs bosons decay into a $b\bar{b}$ pair and a pair of photons, respectively. The analysis targets the $VH$ production mode, specifically searching for the $VH \to Vbb\gamma\gamma$ final state. The results are compared against Standard Model predictions, which forecast a cross-section of 0.15 pb for this process. The study establishes 95% confidence level upper limits on the production cross-section for various $VH$ decay modes, assuming a Standard Model Higgs boson with a mass of 125 GeV.

We introduce a novel laser architecture that utilizes alkali vapor to generate a digital output, where the laser's on-off state is determined by the spin polarization of the alkali atoms. This system operates by employing a pump laser to induce a spin-exchange collisional exchange between the pump photons and the alkali atoms, thereby transferring the pump's spin state to the alkali atoms. The resulting laser output is then modulated by a second laser, which acts as a control beam to switch the emission on or off based on the spin polarization of the alkali atoms. This system has been demonstrated to produce a digital output with a high degree of reliability and stability, making it a promising candidate for applications in quantum information processing and other fields.

This finding extends previous work by Elkies, Elkies, and others, who established a lower bound of 20 for K3 surfaces with a Siegel disk of modulus 1 in their dynamics. We also provide an explicit example of a K3 surface defined over $\mathbb{Q}$ with a Siegel disk of modulus 1 in its dynamics and Picard number 19. This study investigates the gamma-ray spectrum produced by the annihilation of a decaying neutralino, which serves as a dark matter candidate. We demonstrate that the resulting spectrum exhibits a distinct peak at the neutralino mass, $m_{\tilde{\chi}^0_1}$, and that the peak's intensity is governed by the ratio of the neutralino lifetime to the age of the universe. Furthermore, we analyze the impact of the neutralino's decay mode on the spectral shape and discuss the implications for interpreting gamma-ray observations.

We introduce an effective, polynomial-time approximation scheme (EPAS) for determining the genus of dense graphs. This method achieves an approximation ratio of $1+o(1)$ and runs in time $O(n^{2+\epsilon})$ for any $\epsilon > 0$.

This paper introduces a stochastic Newton method designed for distributed convex optimization within a network of agents. The proposed algorithm operates by having each agent compute a stochastic gradient estimate and a stochastic Hessian estimate, subsequently updating its local variable using these metrics. The approach is applicable to general convex problems, including those with nonsmooth components, and accommodates both strongly convex and non-strongly convex scenarios. Theoretical analysis demonstrates that the algorithm achieves an expected convergence rate of $O(1/k)$ for the objective function value and $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for the expected norm of the subgradient. Furthermore, numerical experiments validate the method's performance across various convex optimization tasks.

This paper presents a neural network-based approach to detecting hate speech in Hindi and Bengali, two major Indian languages. We introduce a newly compiled dataset containing 10,000 annotated examples of hate speech for each language. Our methodology involves training a neural network on this dataset and evaluating its performance against models trained on English hate speech data. The results indicate that the model achieves an F1 score of 0.89 on Hindi and 0.85 on Bengali, surpassing the performance of models trained exclusively on English data.

Gas Time Projection Chambers (TPCs) are highly effective for detecting dark matter, neutrinos, and other weakly interacting particles. While traditional TPCs rely on 2D readout, recent advancements have introduced 3D readout systems capable of high-resolution tracking of ionization trails. This capability allows for the precise determination of the initial recoil position and the full spatial distribution of charge and electron drift, enabling the reconstruction of the original ionization track. This paper outlines the observables derived from such 3D data and their application to dark matter searches. Specifically, we examine how these observables can distinguish between nuclear and electron recoils, and we demonstrate that they can be utilized to measure the initial recoil position and the original ionization track.

The commercial driving industry is a critical yet under-researched sector, characterized by a workforce that is predominantly male, non-white, and often lacking formal education. This study introduces a novel framework for evaluating driver performance through a machine learning model that integrates expert knowledge. The system utilizes a contextual intelligent choice algorithm to synthesize data from multiple sources, including vehicle telematics, video footage, and expert assessments. By employing a multi-objective optimization approach, the model balances conflicting goals such as safety, efficiency, and fairness. The resulting system is designed to be adaptable, capable of accommodating various expert opinions and evolving industry standards.

This study examines the geodesic paths within a manifold defined by a Gaussian random field, a structure that emerges in numerous physical and mathematical contexts. We establish a general framework for computing geodesic trajectories and demonstrate its application to a Gaussian random field characterized by a specific covariance function.

This paper examines the distribution of the number of closed geodesics with a given length on a compact Riemann surface of genus $g \geq 2$ equipped with a hyperbolic metric. We demonstrate that, for any fixed length $L$, the count of such geodesics follows a normal distribution with a mean of $L$ and a variance of $L/2$. Furthermore, we establish that the count of geodesics with length $L$ is asymptotically equivalent to $e^L$ as $L$ approaches infinity.
This paper establishes a bound on the denominators of the distinctive values of L-functions for both elliptic curves and newforms.

We investigate the spin-dependent transport characteristics of armchair graphene nanoribbons (AGNRs) connected to ferromagnetic (FM) electrodes. Our findings indicate that the spin-polarized transmission probability is highly sensitive to the AGNR width, the FM magnetization direction, and the applied bias voltage. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the spin-polarized transmission can be effectively modulated by applying an external electric field.

This paper establishes Korovkin-type theorems for weakly nonlinear and monotone operators defined on a Banach space. These operators are expressed as the sum of a linear operator and a nonlinear operator that is both continuous and compact. The findings are applied to investigate the convergence of sequences of positive linear operators acting on the space of continuous functions over a compact Hausdorff domain.

This paper establishes that every connected graph $G$ with $n$ vertices, where $n \geq 3$, and independence number $\alpha(G) \leq n/2$ is pancyclic, provided it contains a Hamiltonian path. This result confirms a conjecture by Faudree and Schelp.

We present a study of directed flow ($v_1$) for charged hadrons across a broad transverse momentum spectrum in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\textrm{NN}}}=$ 200 GeV, utilizing data from the STAR experiment at RHIC. The analysis covers a pseudorapidity range of $-1.0 < \eta < 1.0$ and a transverse momentum interval of $0.15 < p_{\textrm{T}} < 2.5$ GeV/c. The results are compared with predictions from various hydrodynamic models, which generally align well with the observed data. Additionally, we examine the directed flow in d+Au and $^{3}\textrm{He}$+Au collisions to assess the influence of cold nuclear matter effects. This study introduces a novel approach to the spectral Koopman method for analyzing nonlinear dynamical systems, specifically addressing the challenges of high computational cost and the need for extensive training data. The proposed method employs a sparse grid strategy to construct a low-dimensional, data-driven approximation of the Koopman operator, which is then used to generate a reduced-order model. By utilizing sparse grids, the algorithm significantly lowers the computational burden associated with the standard spectral Koopman method. Furthermore, the method incorporates an adaptive data-driven framework that automatically refines the sparse grid based on the system's dynamics, ensuring high accuracy with minimal data requirements. The effectiveness of this approach is validated through numerical experiments on both linear and nonlinear systems, demonstrating its ability to achieve precise results with reduced computational resources.

This study introduces a novel outer complex scaling (OCS) approach designed to investigate strong-field ionization in atoms and molecules. The method involves applying a complex rotation to the outermost part of the real-space grid, while the inner region remains unrotated. This configuration allows the inner region to accurately describe the bound states and the core potential, whereas the outer region captures the ionization dynamics and long-range Coulomb potential. The approach is validated by calculating ionization rates for the hydrogen atom and molecular hydrogen, demonstrating excellent agreement with established literature. Furthermore, the method is applied to analyze the strong-field ionization of the water molecule, yielding results that align well with prior studies.

The Sinkhorn algorithm is a standard iterative method for solving the optimal transport problem, typically converging to the optimal transport plan. However, this paper addresses a scenario where the optimal transport problem is ill-posed, specifically when the associated Schr\"odinger system lacks a solution. We demonstrate that, in this case, the Sinkhorn algorithm converges to the solution of a well-defined, regularized optimal transport problem.

This study presents a measurement of the top-quark pair production cross-section using proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 5.02 TeV, recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC during 2012. The analysis focuses on the dilepton decay channel, where the top quarks decay into a muon or tauon and a bottom quark. The measured cross-section is $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} = 10.5 \pm 0.3(\text{stat}) \pm 0.3(\text{syst}) \pm 0.2(\text{lumi})$ pb, which aligns with the Standard Model prediction of $10.1 \pm 0.2$ pb.

This study examines the localization dynamics of a centrally linked system, where a central spin interacts with a bath of non-interacting spins. We demonstrate that the system's localization behavior is governed by the interplay between the bath's initial state and the coupling strength. Specifically, we show that the system can transition from a localized to a delocalized state as the coupling strength increases. Furthermore, we find that the system's localization behavior is highly sensitive to the bath's initial state, with the system exhibiting different localization behaviors for different initial states.

This study introduces a new subclass of analytic functions defined by the condition that the real part of a specific linear combination involving generalized Bessel functions remains bounded below by a constant $\alpha$ within the open unit disk. We establish several fundamental properties of this class, including relationships with other function classes, coefficient bounds, distortion theorems, and results concerning radii of starlikeness and convexity. Furthermore, we derive sufficient conditions for subordination and demonstrate that the class is closed under certain linear operators.

The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically reshaped human interactions, yet the specific impacts on the diversity of urban social encounters remain unclear. This study analyzes data from 1.5 million GPS-tracked individuals in New York City to examine how mobility patterns and the diversity of interpersonal encounters evolved throughout the pandemic. We observe that while the pandemic significantly reduced the overall number of encounters, it simultaneously increased their diversity. This shift is primarily driven by a decline in interactions within the most densely populated areas, such as Manhattan's Central Business District, and a corresponding rise in encounters in less populated regions. Furthermore, we find that the diversity of encounters correlates with income levels, a relationship that intensified during the pandemic. These findings suggest that the pandemic has not only altered the quantity of urban social interactions but also their qualitative nature, with lasting implications for social dynamics and economic inequality.

This study evaluates the performance of two distinct nonlinear field-splitting approaches for simulating two-phase flow in heterogeneous porous media. The first method employs a nonlinear split of the capillary pressure, while the second utilizes a nonlinear split of the relative permeability. Both techniques are benchmarked against a linear field-splitting approach, which serves as a baseline. The assessment focuses on the accuracy of the resulting saturation profiles and the computational efficiency required to achieve convergence. The findings indicate that the nonlinear capillary pressure split yields superior accuracy compared to both the linear field-splitting method and the nonlinear relative permeability split.

We introduce a new class of chiral optical resonators that exhibit single-handedness, meaning they support a single optical mode. This unique behavior arises from the interplay between the resonator's geometry and the chirality of the optical field. We demonstrate that this class of resonators can be used to create chiral optical switches and modulators, which have potential applications in quantum information processing and sensing.

We investigate the connection between the two-dimensional Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravitational theory and the Liouville conformal field theory (CFT) in the semiclassical regime. By analyzing the Liouville CFT in the large central charge limit, we demonstrate that it reduces to JT gravity. Furthermore, we establish that the partition function of Liouville CFT corresponds to the matrix model governing the JT gravitational theory.

This study examines the Alcubierre warp drive spacetime within the framework of an ideal fluid, incorporating a cosmological constant. We demonstrate that the warp drive metric can be expressed as a perfect fluid solution for both the cosmological constant and the energy-momentum tensor of an ideal fluid. Furthermore, we derive the corresponding equations of motion for the fluid and analyze the physical characteristics of the fluid's energy density and pressure.

The GUIDES project aims to develop a geospatial information system for urban infrastructure, designed to support the creation of new facilities and the maintenance of existing ones. It will also serve as a decision-making tool for city planners and managers. The system's core functionality relies on a geospatial database that stores data regarding urban infrastructure, including its physical attributes and spatial locations. To ensure the system is user-friendly, it will feature a web-based interface that allows users to query the database and visualize results on a map.

We present a method for characterizing the temperature, distribution, and heating rates of motional modes in a two-dimensional ion crystal using spin-dependent dephasing. This approach offers a sensitive, non-destructive, and rapid means of monitoring ion heating, which is essential for maintaining the high motional ground-state populations required for quantum information processing. By analyzing the dephasing dynamics, we can determine the temperature of individual modes, the heating velocity, and the motional state distribution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this technique is capable of detecting the heating of a single mode within a 2D crystal, even when other modes remain in the ground state.

This study presents a comprehensive quantum mechanical framework for analyzing Tip-Enhanced Raman Scattering (TERS), explicitly accounting for both the electromagnetic and chemical enhancement mechanisms. By employing a model system of a benzene molecule adsorbed on a gold substrate and probed by a gold tip, we investigate the influence of the tip's position and the substrate's dielectric properties on the TERS signal. Our findings indicate that the chemical enhancement mechanism is highly sensitive to the tip's proximity to the substrate, a result that aligns with experimental observations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the electromagnetic enhancement mechanism is significantly modulated by the substrate's dielectric constant.

We report on the Sardinia Radio Telescope's (SRT) K-band observations of the nearby galaxies NGC 4258, NGC 4395, and NGC 4449. These galaxies were selected for their diverse morphologies and star formation histories, which are expected to produce distinct radio emission characteristics. The study aims to identify and characterize the radio continuum sources within these galaxies, with a specific focus on detecting non-thermal emission from star-forming regions. The results reveal that NGC 4258 and NGC 4395 are dominated by thermal emission from the interstellar medium, whereas NGC 4449 exhibits a significant non-thermal component. This non-thermal emission is primarily attributed to supernova remnants and HII regions, with a notable concentration of compact sources in NGC 4449. The findings are discussed in the context of the galaxies' star formation histories and their respective environments.

The entropy change ($\Delta S$) associated with the caloric effect in molecular crystals is typically limited by the low entropy of the ordered phase. However, ammonium sulfate, $(NH_4)_2SO_4$, exhibits an unusually large $\Delta S$ of approximately $100$ J/kg K, which is comparable to that of the classic caloric material barium titanate. This study investigates the origin of this extensive entropy change by examining the crystal structure and the nature of hydrogen bonding. We demonstrate that the extensive $\Delta S$ arises from the substantial configurational entropy of the disordered phase, which is driven by the high degree of hydrogen bond disorder.

Reinforcement learning (RL) models are widely used to explain how the brain learns from experience, yet they often fail to account for the diverse, suboptimal strategies humans employ. This study investigates whether these non-ideal behaviors are merely random errors or if they reflect consistent, individual-specific traits. We analyzed data from 100 participants performing a probabilistic learning task, finding that while most followed standard RL predictions, a significant minority adopted distinct, suboptimal tactics. Crucially, these individual deviations remained stable across different experimental conditions, suggesting they are trait-like characteristics. Furthermore, we observed that the brain's midbrain encodes prediction errors according to these unique learning profiles, indicating that the neural mechanisms adapt to an individual's specific learning style. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating diverse behavioral patterns into computational models of human learning.

This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement and contextuality framework based on the complexification of the $E_8$ Lie algebra, which serves as a core system. We demonstrate that the complex $E_8$ core system can be decomposed into a direct sum of two real $E_8$ core systems. Furthermore, we establish a correspondence between the complex $E_8$ core system and the complexification of the $E_8$ core system. We also define a contextuality framework utilizing the complex $E_8$ core system and its associated complex $E_8$ core system. Finally, we outline a strategy for constructing a quantum entanglement framework using the complex $E_8$ core system and its corresponding complex $E_8$ core system.

This study addresses the Close Neighbor Searching (CNS) problem for time series data under the Fréchet distance, a metric widely used to quantify similarity between temporal sequences. We introduce a novel approximate CNS framework that leverages the Fréchet distance, offering a tight upper bound on the query time. Our approach is built upon a new data structure that supports efficient approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) searches within the Fréchet distance space. We demonstrate that this structure achieves a query time of $O(\log n)$ and an update time of $O(n)$, where $n$ represents the number of time series. Furthermore, we establish a lower bound of $\Omega(n)$ for the update time, proving that our proposed data structure is optimal.

Measurement error correction is essential for obtaining precise results in quantum experiments, yet current methods often fail to scale with the number of measurements. This paper introduces a scalable approach that leverages the Bayesian unfolding technique to correct measurement errors in quantum experiments. By employing a two-step process, the method first estimates the measurement error matrix and subsequently applies it to correct the experimental data. The authors validate this approach through numerical simulations and experimental demonstrations on a superconducting quantum processor, confirming its effectiveness in accurately correcting measurement errors.

Shared autonomy is a framework where a human collaborates with a robot to jointly execute a task. This paper introduces a novel approach to robot-human communication, termed "shared autonomy communication," which utilizes the robot's autonomy level as a communicative signal. We demonstrate that this method enables robots to convey their internal state and intentions to humans, thereby facilitating more effective human-robot collaboration.

This paper introduces HiTMap, a hierarchical topological map designed for navigation in unknown environments. The proposed system utilizes a hierarchical approach to construct a topological map, which is then converted into a HiTMap representation. This representation is subsequently employed for path planning. Experimental results demonstrate that HiTMap achieves superior performance compared to existing methods.

This study introduces a unified framework for simultaneously reconstructing polyenergetic CT images, denoising sensor data, and decomposing materials. The approach models the reconstruction and denoising tasks as a non-convex variational problem, where the denoising component is defined by a non-convex total variation (TV) regularizer. This TV term is parameterized by a function that varies with the image intensity, allowing it to adapt to local features. The resulting optimization problem is solved using an alternating minimization strategy, which iteratively updates the reconstruction and the denoising parameters. The proposed method is validated through numerical experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Named entity retrieval (NER) is a critical component of natural language processing (NLP) that involves identifying and locating entities within a document collection based on a specific query. While traditional NER systems rely on static entity representations, this paper introduces a novel approach to contextual NER by modeling entities as dynamic vectors that respond to query terms. We propose a relevance response mechanism for these vectors, which is trained using a contrastive loss function. This method enables the system to generate entity vectors that are highly pertinent to the input query. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods.

Time series data is frequently characterized by its high dimensionality and intricate temporal dependencies, which can hinder user comprehension. While interactive visualization is a common strategy to enhance understanding, it often fails to fully leverage the inherent temporal nature of such data. This paper introduces a novel approach to interactive visualization that capitalizes on temporal characteristics to boost user engagement. We present a framework for designing interactive displays of multivariate time series and longitudinal data, featuring a set of techniques for temporal data exploration. These methods are demonstrated through a case study involving the analysis of COVID-19 data.

Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have recently emerged as a powerful tool for analyzing electronic health records (EHRs) to support clinical decision-making. However, existing GNN approaches typically rely on homogeneous graphs, which restricts their ability to capture the complex, multi-relational nature of EHRs. To address this limitation, we introduce Heterogeneous Resemblance Graph Neural Network (HRGNN), a novel framework designed to model diverse patient data. HRGNN constructs a heterogeneous graph where nodes represent various entities, and edges denote relationships between them. To handle the sparsity inherent in these graphs, we propose a new edge representation method that utilizes a resemblance matrix to encode edge information. Furthermore, we develop a new message-passing mechanism that aggregates information from neighboring nodes based on edge weights. Experimental results on a real-world EHR dataset demonstrate that HRGNN outperforms current state-of-the-art methods in predicting patient outcomes.

This study examines the impact of solvent polarization on the electric double layer (EDL) surrounding a charged soft surface within an electrolyte solution. We developed a comprehensive model that integrates the Poisson-Boltzmann equation with a mean-field approach to solvent polarization, alongside a soft surface model. By solving this system numerically, we analyzed how solvent polarization influences the EDL structure and the resulting electrostatic potential. Our findings indicate that solvent polarization significantly alters the EDL structure, leading to a substantial reduction in the electrostatic potential near the surface. Furthermore, we observed that the magnitude of this effect is contingent upon the surface's mechanical properties and the ionic strength of the solution. These results offer valuable insights into the role of solvent polarization in the EDL structure and electrostatic potential at charged soft interfaces.

Software specifications are essential for the development, maintenance, and evolution of software systems. However, creating these specifications is often difficult and costly, leading to a high frequency of errors. To address this, we propose a method for automatically generating specifications by leveraging unstructured documents such as emails, meeting minutes, and chat logs. Our approach utilizes a transformer-based model to extract relevant information from these documents and subsequently generates specifications using a grammar-guided framework. We evaluated the system on a dataset of 1,000 documents, demonstrating that it can effectively produce specifications for various software systems.

This study addresses the challenge of minimizing total energy consumption in a multi-source, multi-relay, multi-destination network. We propose an energy-efficient collaborative network coding (CNC) framework that jointly optimizes relay scheduling and power allocation. The approach involves selecting a subset of relays to assist in data transmission and determining the optimal transmit power for each selected relay. The resulting optimization problem is formulated as a mixed-integer non-linear program (MINLP). To solve this, we introduce a two-stage algorithm: first, a heuristic method is used to determine the relay schedule, followed by a convex optimization technique to calculate the power allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme significantly outperforms existing methods in terms of energy efficiency.

We present a relativistic first-principles investigation of Yu-Shiba-Rusinov (YSR) states in a system comprising an Mn adatom and Mn clusters situated on a Nb(110) surface. Our analysis reveals that the adatom's YSR states are predominantly localized within the Mn $d$-orbitals, whereas the YSR states of the clusters are primarily distributed across the Nb $d$-orbitals. Furthermore, we examine the impact of spin-orbit coupling on these states, finding that it induces a splitting of the adatom's YSR states into two distinct energy levels.

This study reports the initial search for the rare decay $K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar{\nu}$ utilizing the decay-in-motion method. The analysis leverages a dataset of $1.2\times10^{12}$ kaons collected by the KOTO experiment at the J-PARC facility in Japan. No events consistent with the signal were observed, leading to an upper limit on the branching fraction of $1.65\times10^{-10}$ at the 90% confidence level.

This study introduces a bias mitigation filter designed for distribution-to-distribution scan matching, a technique used to align two-dimensional point clouds. The filter operates by applying a convolutional neural network (CNN) to the probability density function (PDF) of the scan matching distribution, effectively reducing bias. The CNN is trained on a dataset of PDFs generated from simulated point clouds, where the target output is the corresponding bias-free PDF. The resulting bias-corrected PDF is then utilized to determine the optimal alignment between the point clouds.

This study introduces a novel, lightweight, and efficient edge detection method for satellite imagery, designed to operate without deep learning frameworks. The approach utilizes a multi-scale strategy to capture edges at varying levels of detail, followed by a multi-scale fusion technique to generate the final output. The method's efficacy is validated through extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets, demonstrating superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

This study introduces a rate model designed to simulate non-linear X-ray absorption near-edge spectra (XANES) under high-fluence conditions. The model accounts for the creation of electron groups, which are formed when core holes are generated by X-ray absorption. These groups subsequently undergo relaxation via Auger decay or decay into the continuum, and they can also annihilate with core holes produced by X-ray absorption. The model's parameters are derived from experimental data and theoretical calculations. The resulting XANES spectra are compared with experimental results, demonstrating that the model accurately reproduces the observed non-linear spectra.

Modulation classification (ModClas) is a critical technology for spectrum monitoring and cognitive radio, yet it remains vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance adversarial robustness in ModClas by leveraging a generative adversarial network (GAN). The proposed method utilizes a blend GAN to generate adversarial examples that are subsequently employed to train a modulation classifier. Experimental results indicate that this strategy significantly improves the classifier's resilience against adversarial attacks.

Segmenting brain lesions in multiple sclerosis (MS) is a critical task for clinical diagnosis and treatment planning. While deep learning has shown great promise in this area, it typically requires large datasets and extensive training time. This study investigates whether pre-trained models can be effectively adapted for MS lesion segmentation using data from multiple hospitals. We evaluate two strategies: training from scratch versus continuous learning. Our findings indicate that continuous learning yields superior performance, achieving a Dice score of 0.755 compared to 0.711 for models trained from scratch. Furthermore, we demonstrate that continuous learning enables the model to adapt to new data sources, resulting in improved generalization.

We introduce a new method for generating contrast in images, termed "bipolar contrast." This approach is grounded in the concept of bipolarity, which posits that the contrast of an image is determined by the relationship between its brightest and darkest regions. Bipolar contrast is defined as the ratio of the difference between the maximum and minimum intensities to the sum of these extremes. This metric offers a more intuitive and physically meaningful representation of image contrast compared to traditional measures such as standard deviation or mean absolute deviation. Furthermore, we demonstrate that bipolar contrast is invariant under linear transformations of intensity, making it a robust tool for analyzing images across various domains. Finally, we show that bipolar contrast can be used to derive a new class of image enhancement algorithms that are both computationally efficient and effective at improving image quality.

This study introduces a framework for machine learning to identify modeling errors in dynamical systems. We demonstrate that the proposed approach is applicable to both continuous and discrete-time systems. Furthermore, we show that the framework can be extended to handle systems with unknown parameters.

We present high-resolution (0.03 pc) dust continuum observations of the Dragon infrared dark cloud (IRDC) at 850 $\mu$m, revealing a complex network of dense filaments and cores. Our analysis identifies 12 distinct cores, with 11 of them exhibiting signs of expansion. The expansion velocities range from 0.01 to 0.04 km s$^{-1}$, and the expansion timescales are estimated between 0.1 and 0.3 Myr. The expansion rates are consistent with those observed in other star-forming regions, and the expansion timescales align with the lifetimes of massive protostars. The expansion of these cores is likely driven by the formation of massive stars, which injects energy into the surrounding material. The presence of expanding cores in Dragon suggests that massive star formation is an ongoing process in this region. The expansion of these cores may also play a role in triggering the formation of new stars in the surrounding filaments. The Dragon IRDC is a promising target for future observations, as it may provide valuable insights into the formation of massive stars in the Milky Way.

Primordial black holes (PBHs) are a compelling candidate for dark matter, potentially accounting for the entirety of it. This study utilizes the PBH module within the PopSyCLE framework to calculate PBH abundances, focusing on the mass range of $10^{-16}$ to $10^{-10} M_{\odot}$. We examine PBH formation scenarios involving both Gaussian and non-Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations, specifically those with a power-law spectral index of $n_s = 0.96$. Our results indicate that PBHs could constitute all dark matter if they form from Gaussian perturbations with a peak amplitude of $\mathcal{P}_\mathcal{R} \sim 10^{-2}$, or from non-Gaussian perturbations with a peak amplitude of $\mathcal{P}_\mathcal{R} \sim 10^{-1}$.

We investigate the phase diagram of a system consisting of hard spheres with a wedge-shaped cross-section. Our findings reveal that the system exhibits a nematic phase, a smectic phase, and a columnar phase. Furthermore, we observe a nematic-to-smectic transition that is driven by the splay elastic constant.

Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has recently emerged as a powerful approach to adapt pre-trained models, offering a cost-effective alternative to full fine-tuning by updating only a small subset of parameters. This paper introduces a novel PEFT technique called Special Token Adaptation (AdaST), which leverages the model's existing special tokens for adaptation. We demonstrate that AdaST achieves performance comparable to full fine-tuning while requiring significantly fewer trainable parameters. Furthermore, we present a theoretical analysis of AdaST, establishing its convergence guarantees and providing insights into its convergence dynamics.

This study examines the preference ordering of sets, a domain where the addition of two sets results in a third, with the goal of ranking these sets based on their constituent elements. We introduce a new set addition problem and demonstrate that the resulting preference order is contextual, meaning it cannot be represented by a single utility function. Furthermore, we establish that the preference order for the newly proposed problem is not equivalent to the preference order of the classic set addition problem.

This study examines the dynamic and thermodynamic properties of a glass-forming polymer fluid across a broad temperature range, utilizing both experimental data and molecular dynamics simulations. We demonstrate that the temperature-dependent relaxation times of the fluid can be accurately predicted by a thermodynamic model based on the Adam-Gibbs framework. Furthermore, we establish a direct link between the structural order parameter and the configurational entropy, confirming that the fluid's dynamics are governed by the thermodynamic state.

We introduce a new training strategy for transformer language models that incorporates a rejection mechanism, allowing the model to explicitly indicate when it cannot answer a given prompt. This approach is implemented by adding a dedicated "rejection" token to the vocabulary and training the model to output this token for queries it cannot resolve. We demonstrate that this method significantly enhances the model's ability to handle out-of-distribution inputs, such as math word problems, without compromising its performance on standard language modeling or natural language understanding tasks.

This study introduces a new approach to generation in neural machine translation (NMT) that leverages a "look-ahead" strategy. By utilizing a beam search algorithm, the model simultaneously predicts the next token and the subsequent $k$ tokens. This method allows the model to anticipate future context, which is then used to refine the probability distribution for the immediate next token. Empirical results demonstrate that this approach outperforms standard beam search across multiple benchmarks, including WMT14 English-German, WMT15 English-French, and WMT15 English-German.
This paper provides a direct proof of the Kontsevich weights for curvature and connection graphs within symplectic Poisson structures.

We investigate large-$N$ CFTs with a global symmetry, where the symmetry current two-point function is governed by a dimensionless coupling constant $\lambda$. We demonstrate that the large-$N$ dynamics of these theories can be captured by a Schwinger-Dyson equation for the current correlator, which is solved using a resummation of the $1/N$ expansion. This approach yields an interacting CFT that remains valid across all values of $\lambda$. We further analyze the thermal entropy of these theories, deriving a large-$N$ expression for the entropy density that exhibits a dependence on $\lambda$ consistent with holographic duals. Additionally, we compute the entanglement entropy for an interval of length $L$ in a large-$N$ CFT with a global $U(1)$ symmetry, where the entanglement entropy is proportional to the square of the charge $Q$ inserted in the interval. We find that the entanglement entropy density scales as $Q^2/L$, with a proportionality constant that varies with $\lambda$ in a manner matching the thermal entropy density's $\lambda$-dependence.

This paper examines the paper titled "A Universal Framework for Pricing Asian Options Under Markov Processes" by X. Zhang and J. Zhang. We demonstrate that the authors' proposed universal framework is mathematically equivalent to the standard Markovian framework.

We present a new investigation into the diffuse gamma-ray background (DGB) originating from galaxy clusters, utilizing the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) data. Our analysis employs a novel methodology that accounts for the spatial distribution of clusters and their associated redshifts to model the DGB. By applying this technique to the Fermi-LAT dataset, we derive a lower limit for the DGB flux from clusters at energies exceeding 100 MeV, finding it to be greater than $1.1 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$. This value represents a significant improvement over previous estimates, which were based on the assumption of a uniform cluster distribution. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the DGB flux from clusters is highly sensitive to the assumed particle injection spectrum. Consequently, our findings offer valuable insights for future studies of the DGB and the characterization of the cosmic gamma-ray background.
